Descriptor-relative file calls, and copying a child's output into a descriptor.

A write that must stay inside a directory checked once goes through an open descriptor for that directory, so a later swap of a component above it does not redirect the write. Plaintext from gpg or age arrives on a pipe and is copied into a file this process created, so neither tool is handed a path to write.

Types

Drain = object
  p*: Process
  outFd*: cint
  err*: string
  head*: string              ## first bytes of stdout, at most two
  writeErr*: cint            ## errno of a write to `outFd` that failed, else 0
  code*: int
One child whose stdout goes into outFd (-1 discards it) and whose stderr is kept in err.

AtSymlinkNoFollow {.importc: "AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW", header: "<fcntl.h>".}: cint
ODirectory {.importc: "O_DIRECTORY", header: "<fcntl.h>".}: cint
ONoFollow {.importc: "O_NOFOLLOW", header: "<fcntl.h>".}: cint
Refuse a symlink in the final component instead of following it.

proc drain(jobs: var openArray[Drain]) {....raises: [OSError, ValueError, IOError],
    tags: [TimeEffect, WriteIOEffect], forbids: [].}
Read every child's stdout and stderr to the end, then reap it. Both streams are read together across all children: a child waiting to write to a full pipe never exits, whichever pipe it is.
